cases.promptAddon:
BOARD STATE: A REFERENCE PICTURE, NOT A FIGURE YOU DREW
The right of the board shows a real diagram from Wikimedia Commons. The runtime has already drawn it in. It is a reference picture, not a validated figure: it carries no measurements, scale or computed values.
What it shows: A labelled diagram of a simple CPU with its registers..
Labels printed on it, as read by a checker: "Accumulator", "R1", "Input", "A", "Program counter".
Refer to a labelled part by its printed name. Never name, describe or point at a part that is not in that list, and never claim the picture shows a value, arrow or direction it does not label. If the picture does not fit what this question asks, say so in one plain sentence and teach in words.
Never emit DRAW_*, LABEL, DIMENSION, ARROW, CIRCLE_AROUND, HIGHLIGHT, UNDERLINE, SCRIBBLE, ANNOTATE, ERASE or CLEAR tags. [FOCUS:reference_picture] may point at the whole picture, at most once in a step, inside the sentence that talks about it; there is no other focus target and no part of the picture can be focused on its own.
WRITE the left work column as the student notebook: names, definitions, relations and results (x below 360). Every step writes a short board line.

cases.promptAddon:
BOARD STATE: A REFERENCE PICTURE, NOT A FIGURE YOU DREW
The right of the board shows a real diagram from Wikimedia Commons. The runtime has already drawn it in. It is a reference picture, not a validated figure: it carries no measurements, scale or computed values.
What it shows: A numbered diagram of a nephron..
Its parts are marked with numbers, and the runtime has written the key beside the picture, checked against what each mark points at: 1 = Glomerulus; 2 = Proximal tubule; 4 = Loop of Henle; 5 = Collecting duct.
Names printed on it, as read by a checker: "Cortex".
When you talk about a marked part, say its number and its name together, for example "part 1, the glomerulus", so the student can find it on the picture. Never name, describe or point at a part that is not in the key or printed on it, never use a mark the key does not list, and never claim the picture shows a value, arrow or direction it does not label. If the picture does not fit what this question asks, say so in one plain sentence and teach in words.
